The `hypercolor.install` script performs standard post-installation, post-upgrade, and removal tasks typical of many AUR packages. The script also provides user guidance on enabling the service and launching the web UI, which is informational and harmless.

During removal, it stops the user service if active and cleans up system caches, while explicitly preserving user configuration data, informing the user that it must be removed manually. All commands are directed at system maintenance or user feedback, with no attempts to exfiltrate data, download remote content, or execute unexpected code. The use of `|| true` ensures failures do not break package management, a common defensive practice.

No obfuscated code, network operations, or dangerous command patterns (e.g., curl|bash, eval, base64 decoding) are present. The actions are aligned with the expected behavior of a device control application managing hardware access and desktop integration.
